$comment: D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE: the RUN witness for `int main(int, char**, char**)` -- the environment form gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51 all hand the process environment (MEASURED 2026-09-24). One source through every exec format that declares the `argc-argv-envp` verb, each realizing it its own declared way: elf's `stack-vector` block declares where the environment sits (`envpFollowsArgvTerminator`, `vectorSlotBytes`) and a synthesized init computes argv + (argc + 1) from the trampoline's (argc, argv); pe's `crt-argv-accessors` block names the UCRT environment pair and the synthesized init calls them in MSVC's own startup order; Mach-O declares no mechanism because dyld calls LC_MAIN with envp already in the third argument register. The program never asserts the environment's CONTENT, only its structure plus agreement with libc's own getenv (see main.c for the exit-code ladder, 90..95). The `__attribute__((constructor))` calls a four-argument function between the entry and `main`, which is what makes this the Mach-O witness for the trampoline's argument-register park: dyld's envp rides the third register across the initializers. The pie formats are run too, because they declare the verb as well. RED-ON-DISABLE: take "argc-argv-envp" out of one format's `entryVerbs` together with the declaration only it reads (elf's layout keys, pe's narrow pair -- the loader refuses either half alone) -> that leg refuses the build (K_ProgramEntryUndefined); delete the 3-parameter `main` row from c.lang.json -> every leg refuses it at main's declarator (S_EntryShapeNotDeclared); an off-by-one elf slot -> exit 95.
